text:
sara_support: FYI customer CloudDocs escalated — p95/p99 jumped after last night's runtime rollout to v2.3.4. They see p95 ~250-300ms (was ~110-130ms) and p99 up to 1.2s on /v1/generate for long-context requests. attaching short sample traces and a few request ids.

deploy-bot: deployed runtime v2.3.4 to canary (10%) at 1799995000 :rocket:

sara_support: sample trace ids: trace:bc12.., trace:ef34.., request ids: req-cc-001, req-cc-002. Happening for both hosted and dedicated tenants, but reported strongly by CloudDocs cohort pinned to canary routing.

alex_runtime: thanks — can you paste one full curl repro (headers + body) we can run against canary? Also which model + max_tokens? did they pin a quantized variant?

sara_support: minimal repro they provided:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxx" -H "X-Model: redwood/llama-open-7b-q4" \
  -d '{"input":"<long doc...>","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They said requests with long prefix (2-6k tokens) hit the tail.

maya_sre: quick check on metrics: canary hosts show an increase in p95 for long sequence distribution at the same time as deploy. I'm seeing larger KV cache miss rate on canary (cold-start spike) and also a bump in RPC queueing depth for kernel selection service.

sam_engineer: interesting — v2.3.4 included kernel selector change + new quant scheduling and a batching tweak (batch_timeout reduced). Could be interaction: smaller batch_timeout -> more small batches -> worse amortized overhead on long-context path.

sara_support: CloudDocs says behavior regressed even when traffic routed exclusively to dedicated (they repro by routing subset of traffic to canary too). They captured headers showing `x-runtime-version: 2.3.4`.

alex_runtime: can we reproduce locally with a canary instance? steps I'll run:
1) spin a canary node with v2.3.4
2) run the provided curl workload with long prefix and record p95/p99
3) toggle batch_timeout and kernel_selector flags to see delta

linda_support: I've asked CloudDocs to send a small sample dataset and permit a short test window where we route 5% traffic to a debug bucket. They're OK with that.

maya_sre: quick interim mitigation suggestions:
- roll canary back to v2.3.3 for customer cohorts showing regression (safe) :thumbsup:
- temporarily pin CloudDocs routing to runtime v2.3.2/3 (no kernel changes)
- increase batch_timeout to previous value to reduce small-batch overhead
- enable fallback routing to older kernel selector for long-context models

sam_engineer: I ran a quick A/B on local bench: with v2.3.4 and batch_timeout=5ms p95 for a 4k-context sample = 280ms; with batch_timeout=50ms p95 = 120ms. Kernel-selector change adds ~30ms overhead on long requests when cache miss rate high.

alex_runtime: thanks. plan: (a) roll canary to 2.3.3 in the next 10min for safety; (b) collect full flamegraphs + kvcache hit rate + per-request kernel-selection latency for 24h; (c) bisect the quant scheduling change if rollback reduces tail.

sara_support: Customer responded: please roll back, they're seeing timeouts at p99 and it affects UX. Approved rollback.

deploy-bot: rolling runtime canary from 2.3.4 -> 2.3.3 (start) at 1799999030

alex_runtime: after rollback: confirm metrics in 5min. maya, can you watch p95/p99 for CloudDocs cohort? Also capture sample traces for before/after.

maya_sre: watchlist on. initial 5-min window shows p95 back down to ~130ms, p99 ~420ms. KV cache miss rate trending down. queueing depth reduced.

sam_engineer: that strongly points to the kernel-selector + batch_timeout combo. I'll prepare a narrow diff reverting the batching tweak and add a guarded flag for kernel selector so we can A/B without full rollout.

linda_support: relayed to CloudDocs: rollback complete, monitors look better, support will keep customer updated and offer a brief credits package for disruption.

alex_runtime: next actions (owners):
- sam: create a revert PR for batching tweak + add feature flag for kernel selector (ETA 4h)
- maya: run a controlled canary with gradual ramp and per-cohort routing (use 1% cohorts) and collect kvcache metrics (ETA 6h)
- sam + alex: run bisect job on quant scheduling change to see precise commit that caused regression (ETA 8h)
- linda + sara: coordinate customer comms and final verification window (ETA 2h)

sara_support: noted, will update customer now. adding support ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/CCD-1245

alex_runtime: also add synthetic tests that include long-prefix workloads to the canary gating so this doesn't slip again.

maya_sre: will add alerts: kvcache-miss delta > 10% AND p95 delta > 50% triggers paging.

sam_engineer: quick note — if anyone reopens the canary rollout please ensure `batch_timeout_ms` and `kernel_selector_mode` are explicitly set in the deploy manifest. We've seen implicit defaults bite us.

linda_support: thanks everyone. I'll close the loop once CloudDocs validates in 24h.

sara_support: closing for now, reopening if regression reappears. :white_check_mark:
